title: Dynamic quantization canary with automatic failover for FP8/INT8 calibration
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a canary rollout and automatic failover mechanism for quantized model variants (FP8 and INT8) that are produced by the calibration pipeline. The feature must: 1) allow scheduling of small-volume canaries for new quant profiles, 2) run automated accuracy validation against canonical prompt/response suites and latency/cost checks, 3) automatically promote on success or failover to a designated fallback model (float16/FP16 or previous quantized stable) on regression, and 4) surface observability signals and a manual override path in the Console. This ticket covers design, implementation, and integration with the calibration harness and runtime routing layer.
background: We have multiple calibration pipelines producing FP8 and INT8 variants for production models. Past experiments showed intermittent accuracy regressions for some workloads after aggressive per-layer quant decisions. Operators currently rely on manual checks and ad-hoc rollbacks which increases risk and time-to-recovery. We need an automated, auditable canary + failover flow tied to our calibration, eval, and routing systems so quantized variants can be safely rolled out at scale.
goals: Safe automated canary rollout for quant profiles (both FP8 and INT8)
Automated accuracy and latency validation gates integrated with the canary step
Automatic rollback/failover to a validated fallback when gates fail
Actionable observability (per-canary metrics, per-prompt quality deltas, and postmortem artifacts)
Manual override APIs for operators to force promote or abort canaries
non_goals: Designing new quant algorithms (out of scope; use calibration outputs)
Replacing manual enterprise approval flows (will integrate, not replace)
Full integration with Dedicated autoscaling (follow-up work)
implementation_notes: Extend calibration harness to publish a canary bundle containing: model artifact, quant profile metadata (per-layer scale/zero-point hints), calibration dataset fingerprint, and a canonical eval prompt set reference.
Canary planner that can schedule N requests over a time window (default: 1% traffic or 1 RPS minimum) and route only to the canary variant for those requests via smart routing policy.

Validation workers run three parallel gates: (1) accuracy vs baseline using weighted prompt sets and delta thresholds (exact match & semantic metrics), (2) latency p50/p95 SLO checks against baseline, (3) regression detection on output distributions for safety tokens and hallucination heuristics.
If any gate fails the configured thresholds, the routing layer must automatically remove the canary from the routing table and route those sessions to the configured fallback model within 30s.
Integrate with Console: per-canary dashboard including pass/fail reasons, diffs for representative prompts, and links to calibration artifact in storage.
Store canary run artifacts (samples, diffs, eval logs) in retention bucket for 90 days and link in ticket/console for audits.
Expose a programmatic API and CLI to abort, promote, or re-run canaries with different calibration seeds.
Backwards compatible: if no canary config present, behavior stays as today (no automatic routing changes).
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end canary run can be created from a calibration artifact and scheduled to receive staged traffic (dev and staging envs).
2) Validation gates run automatically and report pass/fail and detailed diffs to the Console and canary logs bucket.
3) On a failing gate, routing switches to fallback within SLA (<=30s), and the canary is marked FAILED with failure reason in metadata.
4) On passing gates, canary can be auto-promoted if configured, or require manual promotion. Both flows must be supported.
5) Operators can force promote or abort via Console or API regardless of gate state.
6) Telemetry emitted: canary_id, quant_profile_id, per-prompt quality delta, latency p50/p95, cost-per-token estimate, and final status (PROMOTED/FAILED/ABORTED).
7) Unit and integration tests covering routing switch, gate evaluation logic, and artifact ingestion are included and green in CI.
design_tradeoffs: Threshold strictness: tighter thresholds catch regressions earlier but increase false positives leading to more rollbacks; will expose threshold tuning knobs per-customer/product.
Traffic volume for canaries: using small % traffic reduces blast radius but increases time-to-evidence; default 1% with ability to configure based on model criticality.
Fallback selection: prefer float16 baseline for accuracy, but provide option to fallback to previously validated quantized variant to avoid cost increase.
Synchronous vs asynchronous validation: synchronous real-time checks increase latency on canary path—we run validation asynchronously on copies of canary responses to avoid impacting user latency.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal staging only. Create canary artifacts and run validation harness with no traffic routing (dry run).
Phase 1: Limited production canaries for non-critical models (1% traffic, auto-observe only).
Phase 2: Auto-failover enabled for non-critical models in production (monitor for 2 weeks).
Phase 3: Gradually enable auto-promote for low-risk models and add enterprise-specific gating policies (manual approvals).
Phase 4: Full rollout to all quantized calibration artifacts with documentation and operator training.
observability_and_alerting: Metrics: canary_runs_total, canary_failures_total, canary_promotion_total, per_canary_latency_p50, per_canary_latency_p95, per_canary_quality_delta_avg
Dashboards: per-model canary history, per-profile pass/fail reasons, representative prompt diffs
Alerts: >1 failed canary for same model in 24h => PagerDuty for model owner; any canary failing latency SLO by >2x => SEV2
Audit logs: store routing changes with timestamps, user who triggered manual overrides, and artifact IDs
test_plan: Unit tests for gate logic with synthetic delta examples
Integration test: simulated canary routing that triggers a fallback, assert routing state within 30s
E2E smoke: run full calibration->canary->validation pipeline on a small model in staging
Canary chaos test: introduce synthetic noise into outputs to verify fail detection
Load test: ensure routing table updates scale to 1000 concurrent canaries without performance regressions
security_and_compliance_notes: Calibration artifacts may contain customer prompt fingerprints; ensure artifacts stored in RBAC-protected buckets and KMS-encrypted.
Console links to artifacts must honor tenant isolation and not expose other customers' artifacts.
Retention defaults 90 days; provide admin controls to shorten for regulated customers.
